title: Week 1 of building a battle game with an AI coding agent (Claude): it tested Godot and Unity on my 4 GB laptop and recommended the engine. About 10 hours of my time
author: WordToTheLine
selftext:
**Word to the Line** is a real-time battle game set before radio. You're the general, and you see the battlefield only from where you stand, no mini-maps with little icons for your soldiers. You give orders by speaking them to couriers. Your officers carry them out the way they understand them, and sometimes one takes the wrong hill for a reason you can work out afterwards.

This week was the foundation: which engine. Here's how it went with an AI coding agent (Claude Code) doing most of the work.

**How we work.** In the first session I asked the AI to write the game's premise after briefly describing my idea. I made it ask me questions until the premise was clear. In the second session we went through the same process for a requirements document using the premise document as starting point. Third session was high-level research, and fourth session was breakup of work into major tasks. Then the first real series of work sessions started, researching which engine to use. Over the week that came to about 25 agent sessions and about 10 hours of my time.

**The test.** The agent built the same scene in Godot 4.7 (.NET, C#) and Unity 6.6: rolling ground, a hill, two armies of block soldiers, and a camera that walks through the lines and climbs the hill. It ran the benchmarks on my laptop (GTX 1650 Ti, 4 GB) unattended, waiting until the laptop was quiet before each run and repeating any run where something else was busy. It also recorded the clip itself with ffmpeg.

**What it found.** Frame rate didn't decide anything. Both engines run pretty well for what my game needs, 50,000 soldiers run comfortably above 60 fps. For some reason I couldn't get Unity's tests to run as fast as Godot's and in the end, that was the deciding factor.

**Next week:** The field. Riding up a hill and checking whether you can tell where the armies are from the ground.

This is my first ever game. I am a software developer, but I never had time to write proper games before. I'm hoping with the help AI I can make this long-held dream into reality.
